items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: going out and finding records and recordings and going to the library and listening to LPs of all the players that influenced the players that I had already listened to, you know Fats Navarro, you know Roy Eldridge

ctx.x: I’m going to guess that you have to be prepared not to react negatively when — like a trumpet student and you say “Roy Eldridge” and they have a blank response.

Of course. Yeah, yeah. I mean I kind of look back to when I was their age. You know? There are a lot of trumpet players I didn’t know about, you know, and thank goodness I had teachers that were on the scene that knew who was who and they guided me in the right direction. So yeah I can never really blame the young folk for not really knowing. When they’re in front of me I think it’s my responsibility to, you know, share what I know and hopefully you know light a spark, give them an AHA! moment. They say okay,…

Do you get a sense of — as an educator — a responsibility to make your students aware of the employment opportunities these days — making a living in music. Do you talk about that? Like here’s what you need to know and here’s how you need to be?
